name: The Era of 1-bit LLMs: All Large Language Models are in 1.58 Bits
authors: Ma, Hu, Wang, Xu, Wang, Lin, Luan
problem: Pure 1-bit weights quantize poorly because the +1/-1 grid cannot express that some weights should be near zero.
mechanism: BitNet b1.58: every weight is TERNARY {-1, 0, +1}, keeping a single bit per sign plus a single shared exponent/bits-per-group field - the '1.58' is that structural overhead. Absorption (folding the RMSNorm scale into the following linear layers) removes the normalization at inference so the ternary matmul is the whole cost. This is again an architecture trained from scratch, not a compression of an existing model.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): b1.58 'matches the full-precision (FP16 or BF16) Transformer LLM with the same model size and training tokens in terms of both perplexity and end-task performance', while being significantly more cost-effective in latency, memory, throughput and energy. COMPRESSION RATIO: 1.58 bits/weight (~10x vs FP16, and the storage overhead is in the 0.58). QUALITY COST: the headline claim is MATCH to FP16 - but only when size and token count are equal, which is a training-cost condition, not an inference-cost one. No end-to-end serving throughput number is given in the abstract.
